name: Iubdan

attributes.attribute: the boastful tiny king of the Faylinn in an early Irish adventure tale
laid under a geis to taste the porridge of king Fergus, rescued after falling in

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Iubeda is an Irish hero. In the early Irish tale Iubeda, he is the tiny boastful king of a people called the Faylinn. His tiny queenly wife is Bebo. His court poet Eisirt tried to curb Iubeda's boasting. Eisirt said that nearby Ulster held giants. To prove it, Eisirt went to Ulster and brought back the poet Aedha, who was in fact a dwarf. Then Eisirt laid a geis, an unbreakable demand, on Iubeda. Iubeda had to taste the porridge of Fergus mac Leiti, king of Ulster, before the next dawn. He took his wife Bebo along to meet the demand. The tiny king and queen fell into the porridge. They would have drowned but were rescued and pulled out. Queen Bebo won the liking of king Fergus. He kept her as his mistress for a year and a day. The king of the Faylinn bought their freedom with a pair of flying shoes. Scholars cite this tale as a source for the Lilliput section of the satire Gulliver's Travels.
